item.title: US inflation set to cool in October after two months of sharp increases
item.description: The consumer price index is seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of Tuesday's release ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Vince Golle and Craig Stirling Prices for US goods and services probably rose at a slower pace in October after two particularly uncomfortable months for American consumers. The consumer price index is seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of Tuesday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics’ release.  The core measure, which excludes often-volatile energy and food components, also probably cooled. The survey median sees a 0.2% increase for October, which would be the smallest advance in three months. The agency won’t publish year-over-year figures after it skipped the October 2025 CPI release due to the federal government shutdown at the time.   The October CPI will be the last before the Federal Reserve’s meeting in December, at which investors expect policymakers to boost interest rates. Economists will also assess the finer details of the report for clues on inflation risks into early 2027.  Economists at Citigroup Inc. said in a recent note that they anticipate limited pass-through of high energy costs to goods prices, as well as moderate services inflation.  What Bloomberg Economics Says... “We expect headline CPI slowed to 0.25% in October (vs. 0.65% prior). The core likely softened to 0.24% (vs. 0.33% prior), with both softer goods and services price gains driving the improvement. For goods, used cars and consumer electronics — categories that have faced pressure from the AI boom — saw slower inflation. For services, gains in owners’ equivalent rent are down a third from a September spike.” —Anna Wong, Troy Durie and Eliza Winger  The latest snapshot of inflation also follows Friday’s stronger-than-expected October jobs report. Sustained employment growth has the potential of ensuring consumers keep spending, while allowing the Fed to keep its focus squarely on inflation. Another price report, due on Friday, is projected to show nagging inflationary pressures faced by companies. The producer price index is forecast to accelerate to 6.6% for the year through October, the steepest annual increase in nearly four years. Aside from inflation reports, National Association of Realtors figures on Thursday are expected to show a decline in contract closings on previously owned homes to the lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates stay elevated.  For more, read Bloomberg Economics’ full Week Ahead for the USIn Canada, September manufacturing and wholesale reports are expected to reflect a slowdown in third-quarter economic growth. Manufacturing sales likely rose just 0.1% that month, against 1.5% the month earlier.  That may be partly due to an unexpected work stoppage at US auto plants that dampened cross-border auto trade.  Wholesale sales, excluding petroleum, likely increased slightly, by 0.5%, against a 1.6% decline the month before. Meanwhile, the Bank of Canada will release a summary of the deliberations that led to its first rate hike in three years. Elsewhere, inflation data from China to Norway, central-bank minutes from Japan to Sweden, and growth data in the UK are among highlights. Asia The week kicked off with Australian housing data on Sunday, revealing that home sales and auction clearance rates climbed and offering hopes of a recovery for a property market that has slumped as interest rates rose this year. On Monday, inflation updates from China may show that consumer price gains slowed a tad in October, to 0.8%, as sectors outside energy and AI remain sluggish. Factory-gate inflation is seen accelerating to 5.4%, the fastest pace since June 2022, driven by supply-side reflationary pressure.   Japan also releases producer prices for October that will likely show cost pressures remain elevated, while consumer-price data from India may show inflation above 6% for the first time since August 2023. Third-quarter data from the Philippines are forecast to reveal economic growth accelerated a bit. Australia releases gauges for consumer and business sentiment on Wednesday, with the NAB Business Confidence reading for October likely to be negative for a ninth consecutive month.  New Zealand’s manufacturing PMI for October is due on Friday, with the gauge having stayed firmly in expansionary territory since July 2025.  September household spending data in Japan on Tuesday may show outlays fell for a 10th straight month, casting doubt over the Bank of Japan’s assertion that a virtuous cycle of rising incomes feeding into spending will gradually intensify. Trade data are due from China, India and Taiwan.  Asia has no central bank decisions in the coming week, but the BOJ will release a summary of opinions from its October board meeting. It held settings steady, while declaring that underlying inflation had finally reached its 2% inflation target. That assessment opens the door to another rate hike as soon as December. Europe, Middle East, Africa Third-quarter UK data on Thursday will illustrate the robust growth backdrop to the first rate hike there since 2023. Economists predict expansion quickened to 0.7%, which would be the strongest pace in more than two years.    Policymaker appearances will also draw attention. BOE Governor Andrew Bailey is in Zurich on Monday, and Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli speaks at the “Bank of England and Its Watchers” conference the following day. European Central Bank chief economist Philip Lane also speaks at that event.  Meanwhile, following the close of nominations for ECB president, euro-zone finance ministers will discuss the race to succeed Christine Lagarde at a meeting in Brussels on Monday.  Data in the region include German exports on Monday, Italian industrial production on Wednesday, and a second reading of euro-area GDP on Friday. In the Nordics, Sweden’s Riksbank on Tuesday publishes minutes of its latest decision to raise borrowing costs. The same day, Norway’s inflation reading is due.   Egyptian officials will also closely watch their inflation reading on Tuesday after price growth eased for two straight months. The central bank unexpectedly raised rates in October. Ghana’s finance minister, Cassiel Ato Forson, in his 2027 budget to lawmakers on Thursday, is expected to outline details of a $10 billion economic plan aimed at accelerating growth and creating jobs after years of post-default fiscal consolidation. Russia’s economy is likely to show weak expansion when third-quarter data are published on Friday, according to Bloomberg Economics. Inflation numbers for October, also due on Friday, may show annual price growth accelerated to above 7% for the first time in a year. Latin America In Mexico, both full-month and late-month inflation data due on Monday look likely to push further above Banxico’s 3% target and ever closer to the 4% ceiling. The consensus sees readings just under the central bank’s new fourth-quarter forecasts, delivered with its surprising Nov. 5 quarter-point rate cut to 6.25%.  Colombia’s consumer-price report also comes on the heels of a rate-setting meeting, though in BanRep’s case the board opted to keep policy unchanged and at a much more restrictive 12.25%. Center stage on Tuesday belongs to Banco Central do Brasil, with Brazil-watchers hoping to glean some measure of guidance from the minutes of its Nov. 3-4 meeting. Few policy meetings have seen such a dramatic shift in outlook — from a strong consensus for a sixth straight cut to 13.5%, to the actual decision to hold the key Selic rate unchanged at 13.75%.  But President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s shock reelection and silence on how he plans to get the government’s finances back in order have sidelined the central bank for the time being. Prior to the bank’s Nov. 4 hold, local analysts had marked up their key rate forecasts to the 2029 forecast horizon. In a timely follow-up, Brazil’s October inflation figures are likely to show another move higher from September’s above-target 4.58% print, consistent with analysts’ most recent 2026 estimate of 5.22%. For Argentina, local analysts look for a third straight sub-2% monthly inflation print in October, potentially slower than September’s 1.9%, keeping the annual reading right around September’s 33.4% level.   Less than a year from the next election, Argentina’s economy has skidded into a technical recession and keeping the lid on consumer prices may be a challenge for President Javier Milei. Peru’s central bank meets Thursday, and after 13 straight months of keeping the key rate at 4.25%, Governor Julio Velarde and colleagues are likely to deliver their first hike since January 2023 after October inflation jumped to 5.25%.

Bullion may remain under pressure as markets track US-Iran war, inflation The focus will be on inflation prints from China, the US, Germany, Japan and India. Investors will also closely track speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data

On the Multi Commodity Exchange, gold futures for December delivery gained ₹3,682, or nearly 3 per cent, over the past week to close at ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 08 2026 | 11:48 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Bullion prices are likely to remain under pressure next week as investors track developments in the US-Iran conflict, movements in crude oil prices and inflation data for cues on the outlook for interest rates, analysts said. The focus will be on inflation prints from China, the US, Germany, Japan and India. Investors will also closely track speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data. Chinese economic indicators will be important for industrial metals, they added. Geopolitical developments will remain a key driver after US President Donald Trump confirmed fresh military strikes on Iran, while claiming that Washington had made "a lot of progress" in negotiations with Tehran, adding another layer of uncertainty.

The domestic commodities market will remain closed during the morning session on Tuesday due to Diwali-Balipratipada. Also Read

Correction in gold prices boosts Dhanteras sales, footfalls for jewellers

Dhanteras gold, silver investments grow nearly 4X since 2005: Kotak Neo

Gold, silver correction may fuel 15-35% rise by next Dhanteras: Analysts

Inflation, rate-hike woes to limit gains in silver, may retest $48: Analyst

US midterm outcome mildly positive for gold, but Fed risks persist: Analyst

"Gold and silver's momentum remains down as investors will focus on the inflation data from China, the US, Germany, Japan, India, etc along with some Fed officials' commentary," said Pranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG - Commodity & Currency Research, JM Financial Services Ltd. He said investors would also track progress in peace negotiations between the US and Iran to end the war, as well as Russia-Ukraine peace talks. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, gold futures for December delivery gained ₹3,682, or nearly 3 per cent, over the past week to close at ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver futures rose ₹5,655, or 3.15 per cent, to settle at ₹1.84 lakh per kilogram.

In international markets, Comex gold futures for December delivery advanced $176, or 4.5 per cent, during the week to close at $4,074.9 per ounce. Silver gained $2.6, or 5.4 per cent, to settle at $51.94 per ounce. Mer said bullion prices initially faced pressure from stronger-than-expected US nonfarm payroll data and improving consumer sentiment, which lifted the dollar and Treasury yields. "However, prices ended with a strong weekly gain of more than 4 per cent in global markets, following a sharp rally mid-week after the US midterm election outcome that showed Democrats sweeping wins in both the Senate and the House over the Republicans," he added.

Analysts said precious metals recovered during the week on bargain buying at lower levels and short-covering, although gains were capped by a correction in industrial metals, particularly copper. The rally was also supported by safe-haven demand following a decline in AI, data centre and technology stocks in global markets, particularly in the US. However, bullion futures came under selling pressure on Friday, with gold and silver closing around $4,074 and $52 per ounce, respectively, Mer said. In the domestic market, prices could witness moderate fluctuations, with global cues, currency movements, inflation trends and festive demand around Diwali likely to influence trading.

Home / Companies / News / Adani Enterprises plans ₹35,000-₹40,000 cr annual capex in next two years

Adani Enterprises plans ₹35,000-₹40,000 cr annual capex in next two years The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, including airports and data centres

Adani Enterprises, the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, reported its highest-ever half-year EBITDA of ₹11,958 crore for the six months ended September 2026, an increase of 56 per cent from a year earlier (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 08 2026 | 10:52 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Adani Enterprises Ltd plans to spend between ₹35,000 crore and ₹40,000 crore annually over the next couple of years, with airports, data centres and its proposed PVC complex emerging as the biggest investment drivers as the conglomerate steps up expansion across its infrastructure businesses. "We expect to do capex at a run rate of around ₹40,000 crore. So, we may be somewhere in the range of ₹35,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore, which is the rate we expect to continue over the next couple of years," Manan Vakharia, head of finance at Adani Enterprises, said during the company's earnings call. The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, including airports and data centres, while bringing its large manufacturing investments closer to commercial operation.

"The heavy lifting will be done by airports, data centres and PVC," Vakharia said. Adani Enterprises, the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, reported its highest-ever half-year EBITDA of ₹11,958 crore for the six months ended September 2026, an increase of 56 per cent from a year earlier. Also Read

Adani Ports to acquire Dutch operator Evos in €2.56 billion deal

Adani Ports to acquire European storage major Evos for €2.56 billion

Consolidated income rose 62 per cent to ₹71,569 crore, while profit before tax from continuing operations increased 45 per cent to ₹3,297 crore. Chief Executive Officer Arun Bansal said the company was progressively moving from a "build-out phase to value realisation phase", as investments made over the past few years begin contributing more meaningfully to earnings.

The airport business and data centres are central to that transition. Adani Airport Holdings reported a 52 per cent increase in first-half EBITDA to ₹3,275 crore, while AdaniConneX, its data-centre joint venture, has expanded its contracted capacity to more than 1.2 gigawatts. AdaniConneX signed a new 240-megawatt hyperscale contract during the September quarter. Its operational capacity stood at 94.6 MW after handing over an additional 29.2 MW to customers during the period. The company expects operational capacity to reach 120-150 MW by the end of the current financial year and approach 500 MW over the following 12-18 months, when the facilities are expected to begin generating billing revenue.

Of the 1.4 GW of data-centre capacity being developed, 1.2 GW has already been tied up and is at different stages of implementation and construction, its management said. The airport portfolio, which comprises eight airports, including Navi Mumbai International Airport, accounts for about 23 per cent of India's passenger traffic and 29 per cent of its air cargo volumes, according to the company officials. Adani Airport Holdings handled 21.3 million passengers in the September quarter. Its revenue rose 20 per cent year-on-year to ₹3,786 crore, while EBITDA increased 55 per cent to ₹1,641 crore. Non-aeronautical revenue grew 57 per cent, significantly faster than the 9 per cent increase in aeronautical revenue.

Navi Mumbai International Airport began international operations on July 15. The Management expects the airport to reach its full annual capacity of 20 million passengers by the end of FY28, supported by the expansion of domestic and international routes and the transfer of some international flights from existing Mumbai airports. The company's other major investment is a 1-million-tonne-per-annum PVC manufacturing complex at Mundra, Gujarat, involving capital expenditure of about ₹26,000 crore. Around 60 per cent of the project spending and construction has been completed, and the first part of the complex is expected to be commissioned in the next financial year. The facility will also include related chemicals and chlor-alkali operations.

Separately, Adani Enterprises has completed the expansion of its solar module manufacturing capacity to 10 GW and expects to commission 6 GW of solar cell capacity by the end of the current financial year. The company sold 1,478 MW of solar modules in the September quarter, up 35 per cent from a year earlier. The proposed investment cycle will require the company to balance expansion with project execution and the generation of returns from newly commissioned assets. Management did not provide a specific EBITDA forecast for FY27.

item.description: The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia's tenure ended last month after less than a week ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary

Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia's tenure ended last month after less than a week

US President Donald Trump (Photo:PTI)

Reuters WASHINGTON 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 08 2026 | 9:17 AM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he had asked mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to serve as White House press secretary and called on him to bring some fighters along as assistants "even though some are not from our country."   White, chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a "violent Fighter and Warrior," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.   Trump also asked for six current or former UFC titleholders to join White, including two athletes from Russia's Dagestan region, Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov; Americans Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and "Kayla Harris," likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian native who became a US citizen last year.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote.   Speaking at a press conference on Saturday while in London after a boxing event, White said he would meet with Trump at the White House on Monday. Also Read

Trump names Stephen Miller as chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles

Man with gun arrested near White House over alleged plot to kill Trump

Trump, Qatar's emir discuss West Asia de-escalation; 30 killed in Yemen

China says discussions underway on Xi, Trump and Putin trilateral meeting

US carries out fresh targeted strikes on Iran's air defences: Trump

The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia's tenure ended last month after less than a week. Zacharia replaced Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August.   White and Trump first worked together in the early 2000s, when Trump's Taj Mahal casino hosted some UFC events. But they have become closer allies since the UFC chief publicly backed Trump's presidential campaign in 2016.

Trump in recent years has attended several UFC events, and in June the White House hosted a night of UFC fights as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence.   The White House press office already has a former UFC spokesperson in White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung, who worked for White's organization from 2013 to 2016.
